scope_note: Report only. No question, lesson, asset, manifest or review state is changed by this ledger. It records no Mathematics or editorial approval.

categories.meaning: Wrong canonical or accepted answer, wrong worked result or hint, an item that cannot be answered as intended (missing or contradictory givens, two valid answers but one accepted), missing prompt, or corrupted learner-visible text.
An existing diagram contradicts the givens, draws the wrong relationship, misplaces markings or labels, or its alt text contradicts the figure.
The content key is right but the checker misjudges answers: resolved by the PR 261 checker fix, or needs a checker_config form/unit setting in content.
A hint, title, prompt, stem, alt text or diagram label gives away the answer.
Exact or semantic duplicates, repeated templates or numbers, lesson examples equal to bank items, answer clustering.

Outcome or difficulty mis-tag, out-of-syllabus content, untaught methods, lesson coverage gaps, solutions that skip the key step, response formats that cannot capture the outcome, a diagram that would clearly help.
Mathematics typed as plain text, unsimplified coefficients, math-mode rendering defects.
Wording, terminology, spelling, mark labels, notation consistency, metadata.

statuses.confirmed: Category 1 or 2 finding reproduced against the current files (answers recomputed, SVG coordinates and text measured). Needs a fix.
statuses.disputed: Category 1 or 2 claim that the files do not support, or only partly support. Not relied on; a reviewer may close or re-examine it.
statuses.open: Category 3–8 finding accepted from the audit report as written. Not independently re-verified (spot checks are noted in the record).
statuses.needs_checker_config: Fixable only in content: set checker_config.form and/or the response unit after PR 261 merges.
statuses.resolved_by_checker_fix: Fixed by PR 261 (fix/answer-checker) alone, with no content change, once that PR merges. Still open until then.
statuses.needs_founder_decision: The fix, or whether to fix, depends on a founder decision listed in this ledger.

cat1_subtypes.wrong_maths: wrong answer key, accepted answer, worked result, hint value or lesson statement
cat1_subtypes.unanswerable_or_ambiguous: missing or contradictory givens, or more than one valid answer
cat1_subtypes.missing_prompt: the prompt never states the task
cat1_subtypes.corrupted_text: garbled or template text in learner-visible content
cat1_subtypes.pool_exposure: defective items placed in live pools (course pool fix)
cat1_subtypes.tooling: validation gap that let wrong keys through

definitions.severity: critical | high | medium | low, normalised from each report's own scale; report_severity keeps the original label.
definitions.batch_order: Tier 1: a confirmed wrong answer, unanswerable/ambiguous item or missing prompt. Tier 2: corrupted text only. Tier 3: misleading diagrams. Tiers 4–9: highest remaining category (checker config, leak, duplicate, teaching gap, plain-text maths, polish). Within a tier: severity-weighted affected keys, then category counts.

records.title: Wrong canonical answer: 55-72-89 marked right-angled
records.summary: g4-l2-529 asks whether a 55 cm, 72 cm, 89 cm triangle is right-angled. 55^2+72^2=8209 but 89^2=7921, so the answer is 0, yet canonical_answer is "1" and the solution boxes 1; a learner who answers correctly is marked wrong.
records.scope_note: Item is in pool g4-lesson-02-practice.
records.proposed_fix: Set canonical_answer/canonical_latex to 0, box 0 and state the conclusion ("8209 is not equal to 7921, so not right-angled"); or keep answer 1 and change the sides to a true triple not already used. The report suggests 65-72-97, but that shares both legs with g4-l2-511 (65-72-98) in the same pool, so prefer an unused triple such as 13-84-85 or 39-80-89. The diagram (D3) must be revised in the same change.

verification.method: Recomputed from the prompt numbers before reading the solution; read canonical_answer and solution; ran the current checker and the PR 261 checker (extracted with git archive into the scratchpad) on "0" and "1"; checked pool membership in question_pools/g4.json.
verification.evidence: Prompt: "A triangular support at the orchard irrigation gate has side lengths 55 cm, 72 cm and 89 cm. Enter 1 if it is right-angled and 0 if it is not." Recomputed: 55^2+72^2 = 3025+5184 = 8209; 89^2 = 7921; 8209 != 7921, so correct answer 0. Stored canonical_answer "1"; SOL1 "55^2+72^2=8209,\quad 89^2=7921"; SOL2 "\boxed{1}". check_answer (current and PR 261): "0" -> correct=False, "1" -> correct=True. Pool g4-lesson-02-practice contains g4-l2-529. Recomputation of all 104 G4 canonicals found no other mismatch.

records.notes: Same false triple appears in the g4-l3-508 diagram (D6). Report root cause R3 (no recomputation check) is recorded separately.

records.title: Stem-and-leaf vs dot-diagram keys for near-identical requirements
records.summary: "24 integer scores ... recover every score while also seeing the distribution" is keyed stem-and-leaf (3); "18 whole-number results ... compare clusters and gaps while retaining individual observations" and the 22-mark paired-classes items are keyed dot diagram (1). Both displays keep every value and show shape; no range is given; for comparing two classes a back-to-back stem-and-leaf is standard.
records.proposed_fix: Add the deciding constraint (wide two-digit range for stem-and-leaf; narrow small-integer range for dot diagram) or ask the learner to reject a stated unsuitable option.

verification.method: Read prompts, keys, and the s1-lesson-06 text and decision-guide SVG.
verification.evidence: l2-504/512 key 3; l3-503/510/517 key 1 ("compare clusters and gaps while retaining individual observations"); l3-526/527 key 1 ("compare repeated marks, empty intervals and clusters while keeping individual marks visible"). No value range stated in any. s1-lesson-06 SVG box: "small discrete data / dot or stem-and-leaf"; lesson 06 section 1: "Dot plots reveal individual repeats and gaps in small datasets. Stem-and-leaf diagrams retain exact ordered values." All accepted_answers [].

records.notes: The keys match the lesson's cue words, so a learner who pattern-matches gets them; the ambiguity is in the mathematics of the stated requirements.

records.title: 'Overall percentage change' answers store unsigned values
records.summary: n3-l3-018 (-3.2%) and n3-l3-019 (-5%) ask for 'the overall percentage change' but store 3.2 and 5, so the conventional signed answers -3.2 and -5 are rejected; n3-l3-012 stores 2 (increase) without capturing direction; n3-l3-027 is listed in parentheses.
records.proposed_fix: Reword to 'overall percentage decrease' (l3-018, l3-019) and '...increase' (l3-012), or keep 'change', tell learners to enter a decrease as negative, and store -3.2 and -5; align with lesson-04 (L-05).

verification.method: Recomputed each change with Fractions before reading solutions; ran current and PR 261 checkers on signed inputs.
verification.evidence: l3-018: 500x1.10x0.88 = 484 -> -16/5 = -3.2%; canonical '3.2' (latex '3.2\%'); prompt 'Find the overall percentage change from the original price.'; '-3.2' rejected by both checkers. l3-019: 800x0.85+80 = 760 -> -5%; canonical '5'; '-5' rejected by both. l3-012: 0.85x1.20 = 1.02 -> +2%; canonical '2' equals the signed answer and '+2' is accepted, so no valid answer is rejected. l3-027: 1.25x0.80 = 1 -> 0%; canonical '0', '-0' accepted; no direction issue.

records.notes: For l3-012 the only concern is pedagogical (an unsigned '2' does not show direction); rewording it to 'increase' is still sensible for consistency. Split: keys ['n3-l3-012', 'n3-l3-027'] are recorded as disputed in a separate record.

records.proposed_fix: Change the numbers so the result is non-zero (e.g. Asha 25% more, -10%; Bala +8%: 1.125x vs 1.08x -> 4.2% to 1 d.p.), or reword as 'Compare the two new salaries'.

verification.method: Recomputed with Fractions from the prompt.

By what percentage is Asha's new salary greater than Bala's new salary?' Asha = 1.2x x 0.9 = 27/25 x; Bala = 1.08x = 27/25 x; difference 0. canonical '0' (latex '0\%'). records.title: Tab-escape corruption in solution LaTeX (\times, \text)
records.summary: 14 tab characters in 12 solution LaTeX strings across 9 questions: a JSON '\t' escape replaced the backslash+t of \times and \text, so learners see e.g. '6imesm', 'yimesy', 'texttens', 'rextpupilstakers'. KaTeX treats the tab as whitespace so latex_fragments_render passes.
records.proposed_fix: Replace each tab+'imes' with \times and tab+'ext' with \text (\\times / \\text in JSON); add a validator rule rejecting control characters in latex fields (R2).

verification.method: Scanned every string in the N5 question JSON for control characters and listed the affected LaTeX.
verification.evidence: n5-l2-002 '6m=6<TAB>imes m'; n5-l2-008 '4<TAB>imes3a-4<TAB>imes5'; n5-l2-010 'y<TAB>imes y=y^2'; n5-l2-031 '-3<TAB>imes2p+(-3)(-7)'; n5-l3-002 '3<TAB>imes a<TAB>imes b=3ab' and '5<TAB>imes c=5c'; n5-l3-016 't<TAB>ext{ tens}=10t' and 'u<TAB>ext{ units}=u'; n5-l3-024 'r<TAB>ext{ pupils take }rs'; n5-l4-001 'c<TAB>ext{ hundreds}=100c' and 'b<TAB>ext{ tens}=10b'; n5-l4-005 '\frac52<TAB>imes r(p-q)'. 12 strings, 14 tabs.

records.notes: Root cause R2 folded in here (validator rule). Catalogue-wide scan of backend_resources JSON found the same corruption outside this report's scope: Sec 2 S1 s1-l2-505, s1-l2-506, s1-l2-513, s1-l2-523, s1-l2-529 ('...\frac{..}{..}<TAB>imes100=100'), plus copies in the N5 and S1 review_packets/*/questions.json. No N5 lesson is affected.

records.title: Joined rectangles: answer x = 3 is not an edge length
records.summary: g5-l3-011 says the 9 x 7 and 6 x 5 rectangles are "joined along an edge of length x cm" with outside perimeter 48 cm; the canonical x = 3 is not an edge of either rectangle, so the givens contradict each other (48 is only possible for a partial contact).
records.proposed_fix: Change the perimeter to 44 cm (x = 5, the full 5 cm edge; canonical 5; H2 "Solve 32 + 22 - 2x = 44") or reword to "touch along a common segment of length x cm".

verification.method: Recomputed from the prompt before reading the solution; enumerated all full-edge contacts.
verification.evidence: Prompt: "A 9 cm by 7 cm rectangle and a 6 cm by 5 cm rectangle are joined along an edge of length x cm. The outside perimeter is 48 cm. Find x." Canonical "3"; HINT2 "Solve 32 + 22 - 2x = 48". P1 + P2 = 32 + 22 = 54; 54 - 2x = 48 gives x = 3, but the edges are 9, 7, 6, 5 cm. Full-edge contacts give x = 5 -> 44 cm or x = 6 -> 42 cm; 48 cm is impossible under the stated condition. Proposed fix: 54 - 10 = 44.

records.notes: Also listed in the text-only diagram record.

records.title: Parallelogram given only as "20 cm by 10 cm" (area undetermined)
records.summary: g5-l4-005 equates the trapezium area with that of "a 20 cm by 10 cm parallelogram"; two lengths do not fix a parallelogram's area (side lengths 20 and 10 give any area up to 200 cm²), contradicting lesson 01's warning against using a sloping side as height.
records.proposed_fix: Reword as "a parallelogram with base 20 cm and perpendicular height 10 cm" (answer 22 unchanged).

verification.method: Recomputed under both readings.
verification.evidence: Prompt: "A trapezium has height 8 cm and parallel sides x cm and (x + 6) cm. Its area equals that of a 20 cm by 10 cm parallelogram. Find x." Canonical "22" assumes area 200: 4(2x + 6) = 200 -> x = 22. With side lengths 20 and 10 at angle t the area is 200 sin t (e.g. 60 deg gives 173.2 and x = 18.65). g5-lesson-01 pitfalls: "Do not use a sloping side as the height."

records.proposed_fix: Change the second speed (60 km/h -> 2 h, or 50 km/h -> 2.4 h) and update hints/solution.

verification.method: Read prompt, hints and solution.
verification.evidence: Prompt: "A vehicle covers a fixed route in 3 hours at a constant speed of 40 km/h. Assuming travel time is inversely proportional to speed, find the time in hours at 40 km/h." canonical "3"; H2 "The route length is 40 x 3 km; divide it by 40."; SOL "d=40(3)=120, t=120/40=3". Pool n2-lesson-05-practice includes n2-l2-516.

records.title: 'Factorise' keys are not complete factorisations
records.summary: Ten factorise canonicals (and their canonical_latex and final solution lines) leave a common factor inside a bracket, contradicting the 'completely' in six prompts and, for the four d3 5.14 items, hint 1 ('Remove any overall common factor') and lesson 13/14 explanation 3. A learner giving the complete factorisation is marked wrong today.
records.proposed_fix: Replace canonical_expression, canonical_latex and final solution step with the complete form (2(p-q)(2+3x), 5(p-q)(1+x), 3(x+y)(1+k), 2(x+y)(1+3k), 9(x+1)(3x+8), 45(x+1)^2, 4(x+1)(x+7), 4(x+1)(x+4), 9(x+2)(x+3), 4(x+1)(x+3)); rewrite solutions to take out the common factor first; add 'completely' to the four d3 5.14 prompts; set checker_config.form = factorised_completely; increment revision.

verification.method: Parsed each prompt polynomial and canonical with SymPy; checked equivalence, sympy.factor result and the integer content of every bracket in the canonical. Also checked the other 16 N5 factorise items as a control (all complete).
verification.evidence: n5-l2-504 prompt 'Bamboo signed grouping: Factorise 4p-4q+6px-6qx completely.' canonical (p-q)*(4+6*x); factor -> 2(p-q)(3x+2). n5-l2-527 'Factorise 5p-5q+5px-5qx completely.' (p-q)*(5+5*x); factor -> 5(p-q)(x+1). n5-l3-519 'Factorise 3x+3y+3kx+3ky completely.' (x+y)*(3+3*k); factor -> 3(k+1)(x+y). n5-l3-527 'Factorise 2x+2y+6kx+6ky completely.' (x+y)*(2+6*k); factor -> 2(3k+1)(x+y). n5-l4-515 'Factorise 27x²+99x+72 completely.' 3*(3*x+3)*(3*x+8); factor -> 9(x+1)(3x+8). n5-l5-502 'Factorise 45x²+90x+45 completely.' 5*(3*x+3)*(3*x+3); factor -> 45(x+1)^2. n5-l3-505 'Bamboo non-monic quadratic: Factorise 4x^2+32x+28.' (4*x+4)*(1*x+7), latex '(4x+4)(1x+7)'; factor -> 4(x+1)(x+7). n5-l3-512 'Factorise 4x^2+20x+16.' (2*x+2)*(2*x+8); factor -> 4(x+1)(x+4). n5-l3-520 'Factorise 9x^2+45x+54.' (3*x+6)*(3*x+9); factor -> 9(x+2)(x+3). n5-l3-528 'Factorise 4x^2+16x+12.' (2*x+2)*(2*x+6); factor -> 4(x+1)(x+3). All ten canonicals are equivalent to the prompt but each has a bracket with integer content >1. Hint 1 on the 5.14 items: 'Remove any overall common factor, then use the required sum and product.' Checker: current branch rejects '2(p-q)(2+3x)' on n5-l2-504; PR 261 with form factorised_completely accepts it and rejects '(p-q)(4+6x)'.

records.notes: Four keys (n5-l3-505, -512, -520, -528) have prompts without 'completely'; they are wrong keys because the item's own hint 1 and lessons 13/14 require the common factor to be taken out, and 'factorise' conventionally means completely. Also absorbs the C-9 bullet 'n5-l3-505 shows (1x+7)' and the lesson-findings row 'Lessons 13 and 14 compared with the bank (High)'. Matches ANSWER_CHECKER_FORM_SETTINGS.md (11 incomplete canonicals = these 10 + Sec 1 n5-l3-008). Root cause R-4.

records.title: Hints and solution use a specific distance the prompt forbids

records.proposed_fix: Keep the condition and rewrite hints/solution with a symbol: let the one-way distance be d km; total time = d/60 + d/90 = d/36 h; average = 2d ÷ (d/36) = 72 km/h. Or delete the condition and keep the 180 km method.

verification.method: Read prompt, hints and solution; recomputed the answer.
verification.evidence: Prompt: "Without using a specific distance between the towns, find the average speed for the complete trip in km/h." HINT2: "Let each direction be 180 km, ..."; SOL1 B1: "Let each one-way distance be 180 km". Recomputed 2*60*90/(60+90) = 72 = canonical "72".

verification.method: Recomputed and checked lesson text.
verification.evidence: V = 20x, S = 2(20) + 2(5x) + 2(4x) = 40 + 18x; 38x + 40 = 420 -> x = 10 (canonical 10). g5-lesson-02 pitfalls: "Area and perimeter use different units and cannot be combined in the same arithmetic expression."; g5-lesson-03: "Volume uses cubic units; surface area uses square units." Proposed fix: 40 + 18x = 220 -> x = 10, V = 200.

records.scope_note: All 104 learning items of the four N5 batches. Examples: n5-l1-005, n5-l1-010, n5-l1-002, n5-l2-017, n5-l3-009, n5-l3-024, n5-l1-003.
records.proposed_fix: Write item-specific hints: conceptual stage 1, first line of working (without the answer) at stage 2.

verification.method: Counted distinct hint content pairs across the 104 learning items.
verification.evidence: 9 distinct hint pairs.

records.title: Function notation f(x) used in questions but never taught
records.summary: Prompts use f(x)/g(x) notation while the outcomes and lessons use y = ax + b; the only f(x) in the lessons is one unexplained display line in n6-lesson-04 (y=f(x), y=g(x) => f(x)=g(x)).
records.proposed_fix: Either rewrite these prompts in y = ax + b form or add a short f(x) notation explanation to n6-lesson-03 (reviewer choice).
records.notes: Confirmed in passing: n6-lesson-04 section n6-graph-intersections contains "y=f(x),\ y=g(x)\quad\Rightarrow\quad f(x)=g(x)" with no explanation. Report section C11 row 1 (lessons 03/04 f(x) and composite functions) restates C2/C3 and is merged here.

records.title: Questions tagged to the wrong outcome
records.summary: n6-l1-003 and n6-l1-008 (tagged 6.2) only read one coordinate of an ordered pair (6.1, same as n6-l1-002/-001); n6-l4-010 (6.2) is a plain simultaneous-equation solve with no graph or relationship interpretation; n6-l2-005 (6.4) finds c from one point, the same operation as n6-l2-027 (6.3).
records.proposed_fix: Rewrite as genuine outcome tasks: read y for a given x from a short table/plotted relationship (6.2); ask which listed ordered pair satisfies both relationships or interpret a shared graph point (n6-l4-010); reframe n6-l2-005 as a graph task.

records.title: Graph-reading outcomes 6.2, 6.4 and 6.5 never assessed from a graph
records.summary: None of the 104 N6 questions shows a graph; every gradient item gives the coordinates in text, so "graph of ordered pairs", "graphs of linear functions" and "gradient of a linear graph" are never assessed by reading a graph.
records.scope_note: Bank-level coverage gap across all four N6 learning batches; no individual item is defective.
records.proposed_fix: Author graph-reading items (gradient or intercept read from a plotted line with labelled scales) for 6.2, 6.4 and 6.5.
records.notes: Split from C4 (separate defect from the per-item outcome mis-tags). Report confirms no N6 question references an asset. Ledger: this is a bank-level gap (new graph-reading items for outcomes 6.2, 6.4 and 6.5), not a diagram for every existing question, so it is not counted per question in the diagram list.

records.title: Difficulty labels set too high
records.summary: Eight items are labelled above their demand under the rubric (e.g. n6-l5-001 labelled 5 is one linear equation stated in H2; n6-l3-010 labelled 3 is 72 / 9; n6-l4-013 labelled 4 is a midpoint of two x-values).
records.proposed_fix: Relabel (n6-l5-001 -> 3, n6-l5-002 -> 4, n6-l4-013 -> 2, n6-l4-005 -> 3, n6-l4-016 -> 3, n6-l3-001 -> 2, n6-l3-010 -> 1/2, n6-l2-001 -> 1) or raise the demand; author replacements at the original levels to keep blueprint counts.

records.title: Worked solutions skip the gradient / key step
records.summary: In "line through two points" items the M1 step uses a gradient the solution never calculates (template opens with "known point = a(x) + b"); n6-l4-011 omits the intersection, n6-l5-005 omits the area equation, and n6-l2-024 S1 states the answer "Quadrant IV" instead of the image J' = (3, -3).
records.notes: Spot-checked: n6-l5-002 SOL1 is "18=3(4)+b => b=6" with no gradient line; n6-l4-002 SOL1 "11=-2(-2)+b"; n6-l2-024 SOL1 (M1) "J' lies in Quadrant IV". Report root-cause 4 (fixed v1 solution template) restates this.

records.title: Difficulty 3 items that are one named arithmetic step
records.summary: n7-l3-001, n7-l3-002, n7-l3-009 and n7-l3-024 are d3 with 3 marks but each needs one step the prompt names (19 - 7, 7 x 3, 5 x 1, "double 13").
records.proposed_fix: Re-tier to d1/d2 (and fix blueprint counts) or rewrite as genuine d3 items.

records.title: Difficulty 4 items with routine, method-given demand
records.summary: Six d4 items are routine expand-and-collect or one-context models where the prompt gives the method; this matches d3.
records.proposed_fix: Reviewer decision: re-tier to d3 or add a d4 demand (constraint, unknown to choose, justification part).

records.title: Difficulty 5 identity item easier than the d4 identity item
records.summary: n7-l5-001 ((k - 2)x + 6 = 4x + 6) reduces to k - 2 = 4 and is easier than d4 n7-l4-013 (a(x + 2) = 3x + 6).
records.proposed_fix: Swap tiers or make n7-l5-001 require synthesis (e.g. a parameter giving no solution, with justification).

records.title: Fractional equation tagged as outcome 7.2
records.summary: n7-l1-014 (q/8 = 5) is tagged 7.2 but is the 7.3 fractional skill, and repeats n7-l1-004 and n7-l2-017.
records.proposed_fix: Replace with a non-fractional 7.2 one-step item (e.g. 9 - q = 4).

records.title: g1-l3-001 tagged 1.1 but tests straight-line angles (1.2)
records.summary: g1-l3-001 asks for angles on a straight line in ratio 2:3, which is outcome 1.2, not angle types (1.1).
records.proposed_fix: Rewrite as a 1.1 task (see C-02a) or retag to 1.2.
records.notes: Split from C-02 (report rates the whole finding High); severity set to medium by judgement because an outcome mis-tag alone does not affect the learner's answer.

records.title: g1-l5-001 hint 2 and S1 give a faulty justification
records.summary: Hint 2/S1 say 'the three angles across the upper straight line total 180°', but x is at the meeting point P, not on the upper line; the equation 38 + x + 67 = 180 is right only via a line through P (alternate angles) or the triangle sum.
records.proposed_fix: Draw a line through P parallel to the given lines; alternate angles give 38° and 67° at P, so 38 + x + 67 = 180 (or use the triangle formed by the upward rays and the upper line).

verification.method: Read hints and solution.
verification.evidence: HINT2: 'The three angles across the upper straight line total 180°.' SOL1: '38°+x+67°=180°'.

records.notes: Split from C-05 (different category from the ambiguity in C-05a).

records.title: Difficulty overstated on 19 items
records.summary: Labelled D2–D5 items are one-step or routine (e.g. g1-l4-016 60+45, g1-l3-023 45+30, routine one-equation D4 angle sums, g1-l5-002 one linear equation).
records.proposed_fix: Relabel (and rebalance the blueprint) or raise demand (e.g. g1-l5-005 withholds angle C and relates B and C).
records.notes: g1-l3-031, g1-l2-023 and g1-l3-008 are also recorded in C-08a (answer stated in the prompt).

records.title: First worked example in every lesson is one step with boilerplate check; identical summaries
records.summary: Each lesson's first worked example has a single step and the same verification note; the summary is identical in all seven, including 'construction relationship' and 'with units' in angle-only lessons.
records.proposed_fix: Give each first example two or more reasoned steps and a specific check; tailor each summary to its outcome.
records.notes: Checked: all seven first examples have one step and the note 'The result follows the stated property and satisfies the original geometric conditions.'; all seven summaries are identical.

records.title: Diagram selection is mechanical, not need-based
records.summary: The recalibration script picked a fixed number of items per outcome to receive diagrams and gave every other item the same boilerplate text_sufficient reason, so spatial items stayed text-only while simple items got irrelevant figures.
records.scope_note: diagram_audit.json for the whole G1 bank.
records.proposed_fix: Re-audit diagram need per item with item-specific reasons.
records.notes: Unrated root cause; severity medium by judgement. Verified diagram_audit.json: 83 x ('text_sufficient', 'The relationship and all measurements are fully stated; ...') and 21 x ('diagram_added', 'Selected as a representative visual item ...'). Also covers 'Not verified' bullet 1 (remaining text-only decisions unjudged). Merged repeat across reports; the per-bank 'text-only questions that need a diagram' records carry the affected keys.

records.title: Lesson recall uses a 4-code display scheme; bank uses 5 codes
records.summary: s1-lesson-03 recall codes 1 table, 2 bar graph, 3 line graph, 4 pie chart; the bank uses 1 table, 2 bar, 3 pictogram, 4 line, 5 pie. s1-l1-004 (hourly temperature) is nearly the recall task but keyed 4, not 3. The lesson diagram also omits pictograms (D-03).
records.scope_note: Defect is in s1-lesson-03 (section s1-13-recall); question_keys are the 26 coded outcome 1.3 items that use the five-code scheme (s1-l1-004 is the near-identical task).
records.proposed_fix: Change the lesson recall to the bank's five-code scheme and add pictograms to the decision guide.

records.title: Difficulty inflated on coded and short-arithmetic items
records.summary: Coded d3-d5 single-choice items have d1 demand but carry 3-5 marks; l4-016 is one multiplication; l4-013/l4-014 are short chains; in l5-004 x = 16 / 0.2 = 80 alone, the pie/bar data are redundant.
records.proposed_fix: Reclassify coded items to d1-d2 or add a justification/constraint step; rewrite l5-004 so x must come from the pie and bar data.

records.title: Outcome 1.2 "read a display" items give the values in words
records.summary: The display is described in words with values already given ("A bar graph shows 6 ... 9 ... 7 ... How many for Tuesday?"); no scale, key or sector has to be read.
records.proposed_fix: Attach rendered charts (with forbidden_visible_labels for the asked value) or rewrite to need scale/key work.
records.notes: See also the diagram-candidate list (record "diagram-candidates").

records.title: Outcome 1.4 items reduce to a subtraction
records.summary: s1-l2-014 (2024 - 2021 = 3) and s1-l2-030 (50 - 20 = 30) never involve the misinterpretation.
records.proposed_fix: Ask for the distortion, e.g. l2-030 "By what factor is the 20->50 step compressed?" (3).

records.title: Under-specified prompts (table shape, columns, codes, "the rest", "precise comparison")
records.summary: l3-001 does not say the table is 2x2; l4-001 does not say chess and coding are the only columns; l3-002 uses codes C, R, D undefined; l4-006 "The rest arrived on Wednesday" should be the rest of the before-noon visitors; l3-021 "precise comparison" could suggest a table as well as a bar graph.
records.proposed_fix: Apply the report's rewordings (2x2 table; "each student chooses either chess or coding"; define codes; "remaining before-noon visitors"; "compare sizes at a glance").
records.notes: Checked while reading: l3-001 gives 60 - 42 = 18 for any 4-cell table; l4-006 gives 35 under either reading of "the rest"; l3-021 "precise comparison" is matched to bar graphs elsewhere in the bank (l1-005, l3-013, l4-011) and in s1-lesson-03, so the key 2 is defensible but a table answer is arguable. Not recategorised to 1.

records.title: Decision guide omits pictograms
records.summary: Lesson section 2 and all 26 outcome 1.3 questions treat pictograms as a fifth representation, but the guide shows only four, adding to the code-scheme mismatch (C-05).
records.proposed_fix: Add a fifth branch "Approximate counts for a general audience -> Pictogram" (or a footnote) and update alt text.

records.title: Text-only questions that would clearly benefit from a diagram
records.summary: No S1 question has an asset and there is no S1 diagram_audit.json. The report lists 1.2 display-reading items (bar, pictogram, line, scale, pie), 1.4 distortion items (truncated axes, irregular years, unequal ticks, icon scaling) and 1.1 two-way tables that would benefit from a figure; l3-027 is described as hard without a scale.
records.proposed_fix: Create an S1 diagram_audit.json recording a decision per question; add figures (KaTeX array tables suffice for the 1.1 items) with forbidden_visible_labels for the asked value.
records.notes: Checked s1-l3-027: "vertical scale marks every 5 units ... third mark to the eighth mark" is answerable from text ((8-3)x5 = 25), so not category 1. Severity unrated; medium by judgement. Root-cause pattern 4 (no question diagrams, no diagram audit) is folded in here.

records.title: Excluded values not recorded for algebraic fractions
records.summary: All 26 5.15/5.16 parts have domain_constraints [] and no solution states excluded values, although the 5.15 hint and lessons 15/16 require them (e.g. n5-l3-506 cancels (x+4) without x≠0, x≠-4; n5-l5-505 omits x≠±5).
records.proposed_fix: Add the restrictions to each final solution line (and domain_constraints).

records.title: Lesson cases the bank never practises
records.summary: No negative multiplier in 5.9 d1-d2; no subject in a square/root and no d5 for 5.10; no a²-b² factorisation for 5.12; no negative/overall common factor for 5.13; no c<0 or difference of squares for 5.14; no subtraction in 5.16 d1-d3.
records.scope_note: Bank-level coverage across outcomes 5.9, 5.10, 5.12, 5.13, 5.14, 5.16.
records.proposed_fix: Use the slots freed by C-4/C-5 to cover these cases.

records.title: Prompts ask for working the response cannot capture
records.summary: Three grouping prompts say 'Show the grouping that exposes the repeated factor.' but the response is a single expression box.
records.proposed_fix: Remove the sentence or split into parts (grouped form, factorised form).

records.title: Generic hints, identical within each outcome
records.summary: Each outcome reuses one hint pair for all 13 items; stage 2 never gives a specific next step, and several hints do not apply (5.14 'split the middle term' on monic items; 5.16 LCD hint on same-denominator items and 'brackets for subtraction' on addition items; 5.15 reciprocal hint on multiplication items; 5.10 'subject appears twice' on d1-d3).
records.scope_note: All N5 learning items; specific mismatches on the 5.14 monic items (n5-l1-509, -514, n5-l2-505, -513, -520, -528), n5-l1-504/-521, the ten 5.16 addition-only items, the eight 5.15 multiplication-only items and the eleven 5.10 d1-d3 items.
records.proposed_fix: Write question-specific stage-2 hints (e.g. n5-l2-505: 'Find two negative numbers whose product is 15 and sum is -8').

records.title: Boilerplate worked solutions that skip steps
records.summary: 166 solution steps (every d2-d5 item) open with one of two generic sentences; 5.12 d2 solutions repeat the answer instead of showing the identity (n5-l2-503 '(4x-3)^2=16x^2-24x+9=16x^2-24x+9', also -511, -519, -526); 5.11 d2 trapezium solutions skip '72=12h'; n5-l3-503 skips '3025-25'.
records.scope_note: All 83 d2-d5 items carry the boilerplate; specific skipped steps in n5-l2-503, -511, -519, -526, n5-l2-502, -510, -518, -525 and n5-l3-503.
records.proposed_fix: Replace the generic sentences with specific step descriptions and add the omitted intermediate lines.
records.notes: The bullet 'n5-l3-505 shows (1x+7)' is recorded under C-2.

records.title: Generic hints that do not fit their items
records.summary: One hint pair per (outcome, difficulty) cell (10 pairs for 104 items). The 6.6 d2 stage-2 hint "...then isolate the one unknown coefficient" sits on the four "compare outputs" items, which have no unknown; the 6.7 d2 stage-2 hint "...substitute it ... to find the turning value" sits on the four intercept and four reflected-input items, which ask for no turning value.
records.scope_note: Generic hint pairs affect the whole bank; listed keys are those where the hint does not apply.
records.proposed_fix: Write item-specific stage-2 hints giving an explicit next step.

verification.method: Read hints on cited items.
verification.evidence: n6-l2-501 HINT2 "Keep negative inputs in brackets, then isolate the one unknown coefficient." (prompt: f(2)-f(-1)); n6-l2-508 HINT2 "Once the axis input is known, substitute it into the original rule to find the turning value." (prompt asks for q).

records.notes: Split from C-8 (hints vs solutions). The stage-1 x=-b/(2a) point is covered by C-1. No hint leaks an answer.

records.title: Template solution sentences and skipped working
records.summary: 166 solution steps begin with one of two template sentences; the second promises a check that is never shown; some steps skip working (n6-l3-506 gives y(-1)=2 with no substitution; n6-l2-502 jumps to =1).
records.scope_note: Template sentences across the bank; skipped working e.g. n6-l3-506, n6-l2-502.
records.proposed_fix: Replace the template sentences with specific step descriptions and show substitution arithmetic.

verification.method: Counted solution steps whose first text block starts with either template sentence.
verification.evidence: 166 of 187 steps start with "Translate the supplied function information into the relevant equation or graph feature." or "State the requested exact value and check it against the original function or symmetry condition."

records.title: Lesson 07 graph: axis of symmetry drawn on the y-axis in both panels
records.summary: In both panels the dashed axis of symmetry lies exactly on the y-axis (x = 202 and x = 230), so learners never see an axis of symmetry away from the y-axis, although the text says b and c move the turning point and example 2 has axis x = 3.
records.proposed_fix: Move the vertex off the y-axis in at least one panel (e.g. right panel vertex at x ≈ 290, y-axis at 230) and label the y-axis.

verification.method: Read SVG line and path coordinates.
verification.evidence: Left panel: y-axis line x1=x2=202 (y 55-285), dashed line x1=x2=202 (y 60-278), curve symmetric about 202 (endpoints 62/342, controls 110/294, 155/249). Right panel: y-axis x=230, dashed x=230, vertex circle (230,80).

records.title: Lesson 07 objective 3 promises use of completed-square form not taught
records.summary: Objective "Use roots, symmetric points and completed-square form to locate key graph features" is listed, but the lesson only reads already-completed forms.
records.proposed_fix: Teach the conversion or reword the objective to "read".

records.title: Outcome 6.7 has no graph in any question
records.summary: Not one of the 52 6.7 questions shows a graph. Graph-reading variants would help the roots/axis items (n6-l1-505, n6-l1-510, n6-l2-508, -515, -522, -529) and the reconstruction items (n6-l5-501, n6-l5-505); a new sketched-parabola item asking for the sign of a or max/min would also close the C-4c gap.
records.proposed_fix: Add graph-based variants for these items and a new sign/direction item with a sketched parabola.
records.notes: Unrated; severity is my judgement.

records.title: No 7.6 item assesses number-line representation
records.summary: None of the 18 outcome-7.6 questions asks about endpoint type or shading direction, although 7.6 is 'representing solutions on a number line'.

records.notes: Split from C3.

records.title: 7.8 D1 items give y, so the pair is never solved simultaneously

records.title: D4/D5 difficulty overstated
records.summary: 7.5 D4 items are two one-step solves; 7.7 D4 one substitution with a redundant x-intercept clause; 7.8 D4 give the intersection; 7.9 D4 give the roots; D5 n7-l5-501/502/503/505 are D2–D4 demand.

records.proposed_fix: Cover negative/fractional solutions, non-monic factorisation, graphical simultaneous solution and special cases.
records.notes: Split from C9.

records.title: N7 lessons fall short of the 2,500-character prose baseline
records.summary: Authored prose is about 1,400–1,750 characters per lesson; each explanation is a single ~300-character paragraph.
records.proposed_fix: Add misconception checks, a third example and fuller explanations per method.
records.notes: Split from L1. My prose count (text fields incl. titles): 05 1,759; 06 1,599; 07 1,552; 08 1,559; 09 1,440; 10 1,722 — consistent with the report.

records.title: Boilerplate summary in all six lessons
records.summary: Every summary reads 'Name the mathematical relationship, choose a method that preserves it…', not an outcome checklist.
records.proposed_fix: Write an outcome-specific checklist (e.g. lesson 06: reverse for negatives; open/filled endpoints; test a value).
records.notes: Report severity 'Low–Medium'; normalised to medium by judgement because it affects all six lessons.

records.title: Lesson 09 objective promises non-monic factorisation with no example
records.summary: 'Factorise monic and simple non-monic quadratic expressions' has no non-monic example (and the bank has none).
records.proposed_fix: Add a non-monic example (e.g. 2x²+5x−3=0) or drop the objective.

records.title: N7 questions that need a diagram (none has one)
records.summary: 7.6 has no number-line item (start with the D2 'closed endpoint' and D3 'reversing' families), 7.7 D3 prompts refer to a non-existent graph, and no 7.8 item uses the graphical method; N7 has no diagram_audit.json.
records.proposed_fix: Add number-line choice items, graphs for the 7.7 D3 family and at least one graphical 7.8 item; create secondary_2/n7/v1/diagram_audit.json in the G2 format.
records.notes: Unrated list; severity medium by judgement. Overlaps C3b and C16a.

records.title: Outcome 2.5 items are plain "length x factor"
records.summary: g2-l1-506, 511, 516, 521 (tagged 2.5, problems involving congruence/similarity) are bare length x factor tasks, indistinguishable from the 2.2 items g2-l2-502/510/511/518/519/525/526.
records.proposed_fix: Rewrite as genuine 2.5 problems (shadows, scale-plan route) or retag to 2.2 and author new 2.5 items.

records.title: Hexagon perimeter does not use similarity
records.summary: g2-l3-518: "regular hexagon side 4 cm is similar to regular hexagon side 10 cm; find the perimeter of the larger" = 6 x 10; the 4 cm value is irrelevant.

records.title: Algebra decorative in g2-l4-513
records.summary: Width 13 cm and length 18 cm are given directly, so x is never needed for the perimeter 2(18 + 13) = 62.

records.title: Lesson 01 worked example 2 uses Pythagoras before it is taught
records.summary: g2-lesson-01 worked example 2 computes sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = 12; Pythagoras is unit 4 (G4) of this course, after G2 (unit 1).
records.proposed_fix: Replace with a congruence-only deduction or add a prerequisite note.

records.title: One-step recall items tagged d2
records.summary: g2-l2-501, 508, 516, 517 are one-step recall (x = the given equal side/angle), identical in demand to d1 items g2-l1-504/509/514/519.

records.title: d5 items are not non-routine synthesis

records.title: Boilerplate verification notes in every first worked example
records.summary: All five lessons' first worked examples share the verification_note "Check that every side and angle was matched in the stated corresponding order.", which is not a verification and is meaningless for lessons 04 and 05.

records.title: Lesson requires full justification; bank accepts only 0/1
records.summary: g4-lesson-02 §2/§6 require both square totals and a reasoned conclusion, but every 4.2 converse item accepts only 0/1 (C5).

records.summary: The 5.15 prompts write fractions linearly without bracketing the denominator, e.g. '(5a/5b)(6b²/9a²)', '((x+4)/4x)(7x²/(x+4))'. Under strict left-to-right precedence 5a/5b = ab and /4x = /4·x, giving a different expression from the one keyed.
records.proposed_fix: Render as \frac{}{} in math blocks; until then bracket every denominator, e.g. (5a)/(5b).

verification.method: Parsed every 5.15/5.16 prompt with SymPy standard precedence plus implicit multiplication (the strict reading) and compared with the canonical; inspected the 5.10 formulae by hand.
verification.evidence: Strict reading differs from the key on all 13 5.15 prompts: n5-l1-515 '(5a/5b)(6b²/9a²)' -> 2a³b³/3 vs key (2*b)/(3*a); n5-l2-506 '(3x/4y)÷(6x²/8y²)' -> 1/(xy) vs (y)/(x); n5-l3-506 '((x+4)/4x)(7x²/(x+4))' -> 7x³/4 vs (7*x)/(4); n5-l3-529 -> x³ vs x; n5-l5-503 '((x²-25)/4x²)÷((x-5)/5x)' -> 5x(x+5)/4 vs (5*(x+5))/(4*x). All 13 5.16 prompts parenthesise every denominator (e.g. '1/(x-5)+2/(x+5)-3x/(x²-25)', '3/(x-3)-4/(x-3)²') and give the keyed result under either reading. 5.10 d2-d4 formulae 'q=(3x+3)/4', 'A=x(4+3)/2+5', 'y=(5x+7)/(2x+2)' are unambiguous.

records.notes: Report says 26 prompts 'plus the 5.10 d2-d4 rational formulae'; only the 13 5.15 prompts are ambiguous. Not in report: the n5-lesson-15 recall prompt '(2a/3b)(9b/4a²)' and both n5-lesson-15 worked-example prompts use the same notation. founder_decisions.question: Which money notation should every question and lesson use?
founder_decisions.context: house-rules-v2.json says 'Use S$ in learner-facing Singapore-dollar contexts' (currency SGD), and the Sec 1 N2 audit made S$ mandatory. LESSON_NOTES_CONTENT_STANDARD.md says the audience is students across Indonesia and Southeast Asia and asks for contexts that work across the region. The content currently mixes S$, 'SGD 72', a bare '$', the word 'dollars' and no unit at all, sometimes inside one bank (for example Sec 1 N3 uses S$ in 28 questions but a bare $ in its lessons; Sec 2 N7 uses S$ in Indonesian settings).
options: A. S$ everywhere. Replace SGD, bare $ and unit-less sums with S$, and add a one-line gloss ('S$ means Singapore dollars') in the first lesson that uses money.
B. Currency-neutral money: write amounts as '72 dollars' or use non-money quantities, so no country is implied.
C. Regional currencies (Rp, RM, ₱, S$, ฿) chosen to match each context, with the currency named in words.
founder_decisions.recommendation: A. The target is a Singapore-run scholarship test, most money items already use S$, and it is the smallest change. Whatever you choose, apply one notation bank-wide and tell learners to type only the number (the PR 261 checker still rejects a currency symbol typed before the number).

founder_decisions.topic: Language variety, terminology and local contexts
founder_decisions.question: Which English variety, terms and contexts are the house standard?
founder_decisions.context: house-rules-v2.json sets locale en-SG and 'Singapore/British English'; the audience standard asks for clear international English with unfamiliar terms explained. Reports flag British spellings (colour, litres), Singapore-classroom terms used without a gloss (highest common factor vs GCF/FPB, trapezium, co-interior, dot diagram vs dot plot, ordinate, travelator, pupil-days), Singapore-only contexts (9% GST, Singapore stamps, house teams) and blueprints that still say 'Singapore G3 Mathematics'.
options: A. Keep British spelling, relabel the house variety 'international English (British spelling)', keep Singapore syllabus terms but gloss each on first use, and replace or explain Singapore-only contexts.
B. Keep en-SG exactly as the house rules say (no glosses needed beyond what exists).
C. Switch to US spelling and international terms (GCF, trapezoid, dot plot) throughout.
founder_decisions.recommendation: A. British spelling is accepted as international English, the syllabus terms are what the target test uses, and a gloss costs one sentence per term. Update house rules to v3 and rename the blueprints so future batches follow the same rule.

founder_decisions.question: For each topic the audits flagged as outside the catalogue outcomes or untaught, should items be rewritten in scope, kept with new teaching, or moved out of assessed pools?
founder_decisions.context: The repository catalogue lists Secondary 1–2 outcomes only, so several of these calls rely on the auditors' knowledge of the Singapore syllabus rather than on repository files.
options: A. Rewrite to in-scope methods (for example, list outcomes instead of multiplying probabilities; remove composition; solve liquid depth from the cone formula).
B. Keep the topic, add a taught section and worked example to the lesson, and record the scope extension in the blueprint.
C. Keep the items but move them to an enrichment pool that is excluded from checkpoints and diagnostics.
founder_decisions.recommendation: A by default, especially for items in checkpoint or diagnostic pools. Choose B only for a topic you know the scholarship test assesses at Sec 3 entry. The strongest candidates for B are area/volume scale factors (Sec 2 G2/G5) and standard form (Sec 1 N1). Please rule topic by topic.

founder_decisions.question: Should the approved Sec 1 N2 batches (b001–b004) and reviewed N2 lessons be reopened for the audit findings?
founder_decisions.context: The Sec 1 N2 audit recomputed all 104 answers and the lesson examples and found them correct; there is no category 1 or 2 finding. The open findings are medium/low: 2 hint leaks (n2-l4-014; n2-l3-009/016), duplicates (n2-l1-002/013, n2-l3-014/022, n2-l4-012/016, a lesson example equal to n2-l2-025), outcome and difficulty tags (n2-l5-001/003, linked-ratio teaching gap), 32 plain-text fraction prompts and 3 'SGD' items. The mixed-number mis-marking ('2 1/2' read as 21/2) is fixed by PR 261 with no content change. Reopening changes the review fingerprint, so Mathematics and editorial approval must be recorded again. The claim CLI refuses approved batches, so each batch must first return to changes_requested in a reviewed PR (b001, b003 and b004 still hold active review claims; b002 has none).
options: A. Leave N2 approved and log the findings for the next scheduled revision.
B. Targeted reopen after the higher-priority batches: fix the hint leaks, duplicates, outcome/difficulty tags and SGD items only, then re-review.
C. Full reopen, including converting the 32 plain-text fraction prompts to inline maths.
founder_decisions.recommendation: B, scheduled after the 72 ranked batches in this ledger. The duplicates and hint leaks sit in checkpoint and reserve pools, so they affect measurement, but nothing is wrong enough to pull approved content now. Fold the plain-text maths into the same pass only if D1/D2 also require edits.

founder_decisions.topic: How much a stage-2 hint may reveal
founder_decisions.question: May a stage-2 hint state the complete final calculation?
founder_decisions.context: House rules v2 say neither hint may state the final answer. Many difficulty 1–2 hints state the full calculation with both operands (Sec 1 N4: 48 items; G5: 53; N6: 13; N7 7.4: 18; Sec 2 G2: one-step d1 items where any setup is the answer). Hints that state the answer outright are recorded separately as answer leaks and are not part of this decision.
options: A. Strict: stage 2 gives the method or setup but never the complete final operation (rewrite about 130 hints plus most Sec 2 G2 difficulty 1 hints).
B. Graded: d1–d2 may show the full operation; d3 and above may not give the simplified result or a value that ends the task.
C. Leave as is.
founder_decisions.recommendation: B. It matches how one-step items work and focuses rewriting on the higher-difficulty items where leakage changes what is measured.

founder_decisions.topic: Response formats for choice and justification outcomes
founder_decisions.question: How should outcomes that ask for a choice or a justification be answered?
founder_decisions.context: Statistics representation and measure choices are answered with numeric codes ('1 for mean, 2 for median…'; Sec 1 S1 31 items, Sec 2 S1 39 items) and the Pythagoras converse with 0/1 (Sec 2 G4, 28 items). These cannot capture the justification the outcome asks for, and several coded items have two valid codes. The G4 converse diagrams also show a right-angle marker on triangles that are not right-angled, or give the answer away when they are.
options: A. Add a proper multiple-choice response type with labelled options, and keep reasoning items as choose-then-compute (for example, ask for a² + b² and c² before the yes/no).
B. Keep numeric codes and 0/1 but rewrite every prompt so exactly one code is defensible; make converse items text-only.
C. Keep the current format.
founder_decisions.recommendation: B now (it is needed anyway to clear the category 1 ambiguous-key findings), with A as a product follow-up. Converse items should be text-only or use a diagram with no right-angle marker.

founder_decisions.question: Does the 2,500-character lesson baseline mean learner-visible text?
founder_decisions.context: The validator measures len(json.dumps(sections)), so lessons pass on JSON overhead. Measured as visible text, 34 lessons across both courses are below 2,500 characters (for example, Sec 1 N2 lessons are about 1,700–1,900).
options: A. Yes: change the metric to visible text and extend the short lessons.
B. Keep the JSON metric but lower the visible-text expectation in the standard.
C. Keep both as they are.
founder_decisions.recommendation: A, but extend lessons where a teaching gap is already recorded (missing worked examples) rather than padding for length.

founder_decisions.topic: Patch or regenerate the templated Sec 2 banks
founder_decisions.question: Should the template-generated Sec 2 banks be patched item by item or regenerated?
founder_decisions.context: Sec 2 N5, N6 and S1 put generator codenames in every prompt and title; N7 puts them in every title. G2, G4 and G5 draw diagrams from fixed templates whose renderers are not in the repository, and 15 of the 19 learning banks were generated wholly or mostly under prompt v1 (all but Sec 1 N1 and N3 and Sec 2 N7 and S1; Sec 1 N2 has one v2 batch), several with templated, non-functional contexts. Patching fixes the verified defects quickly; regenerating would also remove the template repetition but needs a full re-review.
options: A. Patch: fix category 1–3 items, strip codename prefixes, and hand-author revisioned SVGs.
B. Regenerate whole banks under prompt v2 and house rules v2 with a data-driven renderer, then re-review.
C. Hybrid: patch categories 1–3 now; build the renderer and regenerate diagrams next; rewrite templated contexts and duplicates in a later pass.
founder_decisions.recommendation: C. It removes wrong or misleading content first without waiting for tooling.

founder_decisions.question: How strict should numeric answer checking be about form?
founder_decisions.context: exact_numeric accepts any equal value, so 'simplest form', 'as a decimal' and 'index notation' demands are not enforced (Sec 1 N1, Sec 2 S2: 69 parts). rounded_dp rejects an integer typed for an exact answer (Sec 2 G4). PR 261 leaves open: percentage-point parts still read '6%' as 0.06, a decimal comma is a format error, and format errors count as wrong attempts. Thousands separators are written three ways.
options: A. Enforce form only where the prompt demands it (add form settings for numeric parts), accept '6%' on percentage-point parts, and do not count format errors as attempts.
B. Accept any equal value everywhere and remove form demands from prompts.
C. Leave the checker as PR 261 makes it.
founder_decisions.recommendation: A. Keep the prompt and the marking consistent; reword prompts where enforcement is not worth building.
